newsitem.title: USA: Moody's rates Milwaukee baseball stadium deal MIG1.
newsitem.headline: Moody's rates Milwaukee baseball stadium deal MIG1.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service on Wednesday gave a MIG1 rating to $160 million of sales tax revenue bonds to be sold later this month to help finance a $250 million stadium for the Milwaukee Brewers baseball team.

The highly unusual deal involves the sale of convertible option bonds with mandatory tender dates anytime following the sale until Dec. 15, 1997, according to Yaffa Rattner, an assistant vice president at Moody's.

Rattner said the MIG1 rating was largely based on the strength of the escrow agreement, which calls for all the bond proceeds to be placed into a guarenteed investment contract provided by triple-A rated Bayerische Landesanstalt. Rattner said the GIC is expected to provide enough interest to make interest payments on the bonds until their tender.

However, none of the bond proceeds can be spent by the Southeast Wisconsin Professional Baseball Park District, a state-created entity charged with financing and building the new ballpark, according to Rattner.
She explained that once the bonds are tendered, the deal would be remarketed as long-term bonds. Up until then, no proceeds from the bond issue can be expended, even for issuance costs, she said.

Rattner said the issue was structured to deal with pending litigation and concerns about the reintroduction of a bill in January by U.S. Sen. Patrick Moynihan that would ban the use of tax-exempt bonds for professional sports stadiums. That bill is expected to include a retroactive date for stadium deals.
She said Moody's MIG1 rating did not "speak to the credit quality of the (baseball) district" or address the lawsuit.

A lawsuit, brought by a group of Milwaukee area taxpayers, is currently pending in the U.S. Appeals Court in Chicago, after being dismissed by a federal judge in Milwaukee. The group is challenging the constitutionality of a 0.1 percent, five-county sales tax that is slated to back the $160 million bond issue.
The Wisconsin Supreme Court has upheld the constitutionality of the tax. The taxpayers are also considering filing another case in state court in attempt to block the bond sale.
